_meta.notes: Android static-analysis rules. The engine implements the checks; this table owns the judgement (severity, CWE, detail, remediation) so operators can tune it without a rebuild. Override with DROID_RULES=<path>.

rules.title: Application is debuggable
rules.detail: android:debuggable="true" lets any user with adb attach a debugger, read app memory, and run code as the app. Release builds must not ship it.
rules.remediation: Remove android:debuggable from the release manifest (it is injected by debug build types only).

rules.title: Application data is backup-able
rules.detail: android:allowBackup is not false, so the app's private data can be extracted with `adb backup` (device access required). On Android 12+ this is partly restricted, and auto-backup to cloud is separate.
rules.remediation: Set android:allowBackup="false", or scope what is included with android:dataExtractionRules / android:fullBackupContent.

rules.title: Cleartext HTTP traffic permitted
rules.detail: android:usesCleartextTraffic="true" allows unencrypted HTTP. On a hostile network this exposes and permits tampering with all app traffic.
rules.remediation: Remove the attribute (default is false since API 28) or add a network security config that pins exceptions.

rules.title: No network security config
rules.detail: The app declares no android:networkSecurityConfig, so there is no certificate pinning or cleartext policy the app controls. This is a hardening gap, not a vulnerability by itself.
rules.remediation: Add a network security config with cleartext disabled and pins for sensitive hosts.

rules.title: Legacy external storage requested
rules.detail: android:requestLegacyExternalStorage="true" opts out of scoped storage, widening the shared-storage attack surface on Android 10.
rules.remediation: Migrate to scoped storage and remove the flag.

rules.title: Minimum SDK below 24
rules.detail: minSdkVersion below 24 supports platforms that no longer receive security patches and predate many modern mitigations.
rules.remediation: Raise minSdkVersion to a currently supported API level.

rules.title: Target SDK below 31
rules.detail: targetSdkVersion below 31 keeps implicit-export semantics and skips several platform security defaults (exported requirement, pending-intent mutability, backup restrictions).
rules.remediation: Raise targetSdkVersion to a currently required level (Google Play requires API 36 as of Aug 2026).

rules.title: Exported activity without a permission guard
rules.detail: The activity is reachable by any other app on the device. If it exposes privileged functionality or accepts parameters, another app can drive it.
rules.remediation: Set android:exported="false" unless external invocation is required; otherwise gate it with a signature-level permission.

rules.title: Exported service without a permission guard
rules.detail: Any app can bind to or start this service, reaching whatever it exposes.
rules.remediation: Set android:exported="false" or require a signature-level permission.

rules.title: Exported broadcast receiver without a permission guard
rules.detail: Any app can send broadcasts to this receiver, invoking its logic with attacker-controlled intent extras.
rules.remediation: Set android:exported="false" or gate it with a permission.

rules.title: Exported content provider without a permission guard
rules.detail: Any app can query or modify this provider's data. Providers are the highest-impact exported component: they carry data and sometimes file access.
rules.remediation: Set android:exported="false", or require read/write permissions.

rules.title: Exported provider grants URI permissions
rules.detail: The provider is exported and allows URI permission grants. Combined with weak path handling this is the classic content-provider path traversal.
rules.remediation: Validate canonical paths against an allowlist, avoid openFile with unchecked segments, and keep the provider unexported if possible.

rules.title: Component implicitly exported by an intent filter
rules.detail: The component has an intent filter and does not declare android:exported. Before API 31 that made it exported; from API 31 the attribute is required, so this app is relying on legacy behaviour.
rules.remediation: Declare android:exported explicitly on every component with an intent filter.

rules.title: Requests a dangerous or high-impact permission
rules.detail: The app requests a permission that materially widens what a compromise of the app gives an attacker. Context for the rest of the report, not a defect on its own.
rules.remediation: Confirm each high-impact permission is required for a user-facing feature.
